title: Consequences if you hole out with a wrong ball
question: If you putt a wrong ball into the hole on the green and do not fix your mistake before starting the next hole or leaving the green (in stroke play), what can happen?

choices.text: Nothing, you continue the round as normal
You get a two-stroke penalty, but keep playing
You may be disqualified for not correcting the mistake
You subtract two strokes from your score

explanation: If you do not correct the mistake of holing out with a wrong ball in stroke play, you can be disqualified.

juniorVersion.title: What Happens if You Finish a Hole with the Wrong Ball?
juniorVersion.question: You putt the wrong ball into the hole on the green. You don’t fix it before you start the next hole or leave the green. What can happen?

choices.text: Nothing happens, just keep playing as usual
You get a two-shot penalty but keep playing
You might have to stop playing and are out of the match
You take away two shots from your score

juniorVersion.explanation: If you putt the wrong ball into the hole and don’t fix it before you start the next hole or leave the green, you can be out of the competition for that round.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A ball that is not yours or not the one you were meant to play.
The smooth area with short grass around the hole.
A gentle hit to roll the ball along the green toward the hole.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Remind juniors to mark their balls and always check before playing on the green.
likelyMisconceptions: Some might think nothing happens or you only get a few extra shots, but you can be out of the round if you do not correct it.
